title: Multi-Party Negotiation and Coalitions
description: When three or more parties are at the table, dynamics shift. Coalitions form, agendas are weaponized, and the person who structures the conversation often controls the outcome.

sections.title: What It Is
sections.content: When three or more parties are at the table, dynamics shift. Coalitions form, agendas are weaponized, and the person who structures the conversation often controls the outcome.

sections.title: How It Actually Appears
content: At a conference, two groups align before the formal meeting to block a third.
A project manager who sets the agenda decides which issues are discussed first, shaping the entire outcome.
'We'll only agree if the other party also gives X'—they become a holdout extracting ransom.

sections.title: Warning Signs
content: Side conversations and private chats before breaks.
A party refusing to speak until others move first.
The agenda seems to favor one group's interests heavily.

sections.title: Protection Strategy
content: Map the interests of every party before the meeting. Identify who might ally, who will be isolated, and what you can offer to build a coalition.
Propose the agenda yourself or negotiate it early.
Don't be the last party left out; touch base with others individually beforehand.

sections.title: Key Insight
sections.content: In multi-party deals, the real negotiation often happens in the hallway before the official meeting begins.
